claims.title: Dirichlet fibre coupling, whole finite observations and exact rounding boundaries

quoted_fields.interface: Known positive Dirichlet parameters a or alpha, nonnegative shape increments b, arbitrary coupled finite-dimensional count indices n,nprime and frequency vectors on the same simplex. Conditional categorical rows have entire mixture-of-product laws. Random rounding uses its explicitly stated known-parameter observation kernel, not a deterministic rounding target. The small-time counterexample is the ordinary two-allele Wright-Fisher diffusion begun at the interior point1/2, with fixed finite smooth drift, positive mutation and diffusion coefficient sqrt(x(1-x)); grid precision b>=1 is fixed in the limit. Unknown source-law sampling access, arbitrary adaptive observations and finite-population chemical chains are different contracts.
quoted_fields.failure: Transportation/Wasserstein-L1 bounds do not imply TV closeness of continuous latent laws. Small differences in total count alone do not control mixture composition; the common coordinatewise count is essential. Whole finite-observation TV is an explicit changed output contract, not an unknown-law probability/ratio oracle or the sample-only N1792 coupler. RANDOM grid rounding has a different law from deterministic rounding. Returning the initial deterministic bin has limiting TV error1/2 at the stated interior boundary; this defeats that shortcut, not all short-time simulators.
